de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment')
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que) · also que — than, after a comparative (mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him') · also que — what (indirect interrogative; dezir vos he que faze 'I shall tell you what he does'; = qué)
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later'
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora)
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
sopo: saber — he learned, found out (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = supo)
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
bivar: Bivar — Vivar, the Cid's home village just north of Burgos
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it')
tornós: tornar + se — she turned back (tornó + -s(e): after a stressed vowel -se shrinks to -s) · also tornarse a + inf. 'to set to, begin' (tornós a sonrisar 'he broke into a smile', perhaps 'smiled again'; the Cid the subject) · also he turned (toward) (tornós a essa part 'he turned that way', the Cid the subject)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront')
alegrar: alegrar — to rejoice (infinitive, reflexive sense 'rejoice, be glad', the se carried by conpeçós; = alegrarse)
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
su: su — his, her, its · also su — their (aquella su almofalla 'that host of theirs')
boca: boca — mouth (besóle la boca 'he kissed his mouth'; = boca)
conpeçó: començar — he began (preterite 3rd sg.; conpeçó de espolonar 'he began to spur'; = comenzó)
fablar: fablar — to speak (infinitive; = hablar, note f-)
qui: qui — he who, whoever (old relative pronoun, Latin qui; = quien) · also qui — who? (interrogative; ¿qui los podrié contar? 'who could count them?'; = quién)
enbía: enbiar — he sends (present 3rd sg.; enbía esta presentaja 'he sends this gift'; = envía)
tal: tal — such; por tal 'for such a reason, for this purpose' (= tal)
tú: tú — thou, you (2nd sg. subject pronoun; used in prayer to God)
muño: Muño — personal name (Muño Gustioz, a vassal of the Cid; = Munio, an old name; Nuño is probably related)
gustioz: Gustioz — patronymic 'son of Gustio' (Muño Gustioz, the Cid's retainer, brought up in his household; = Gustioz, no modern form)
per: Per — Pero, short for Pedro (Per Vermudoz = Pedro Bermúdez, a vassal of the Cid)
delant: delant — ahead, in front (apocopated adverb; = delante)
martín: Martín (Antolínez) — a knight of Burgos, companion of the Cid, who provisions him on his exile and negotiates the loan from Raquel and Vidas · also río Martín — the river Martín, in Aragon (el val de río Martín 'the valley of the river Martín'; = río Martín)
antolínez: Antolínez — surname of Martín Antolínez, the Burgalese knight who aids the Cid
un: uno — a, one (apocopated masc. before a noun)
burgalés: burgalés — a man of Burgos (noun/adj.; el Burgalés, an epithet of Martín Antolínez)
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection') · 'whereof, with which' (Pidal 'de lo cual'; don yo sea pagado 'whereof I may be satisfied')
jerome: Jerome — Jerónimo, the Cid's bishop of Valencia (Pidal restores Jero[me], 'don Jerome'; = Jerónimo)
coronado: coronado — tonsured one, cleric (past part. used as noun; 'un coronado' is a priest with the tonsure 'crown' shaved on his head; modern coronado = 'crowned', so the sense differs; Pidal: 'clérigo'; = clérigo)
prestar: prestar — to be worth, avail (infinitive; cavallero de prestar 'a knight of worth'; = valer)
guisados: guisar — made ready, prepared (past part. masc. pl.; de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go'; = dispuestos)
huebos: huebos — need (Latin opus); huebos (me) ser/aver = 'to have need (of)'
lidiar: lidiar — to fight (infinitive; = lidiar, closest luchar)
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count' · also por — as (por heredad 'as a possession')
santa: santo — Saint (fem.); Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos · santa — holy (adjective; santa Trinidad 'the Holy Trinity', santa María madre 'holy Mary, (thy) mother', the Virgin)
maría: María — Mary; Santa María, the cathedral of Burgos
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
passar: passar — to cross, pass over (infinitive; = pasar) · also passar — 'to pass through, pierce' (tanta adágara foradar e passar 'so many shields pierced and passed through') · also noun el passar 'the crossing' (en el passar de Xúcar 'at the crossing of the Júcar'; = el paso)
molina: Molina — Molina (de Aragón), town in the province of Guadalajara (= Molina)
más: más — more; e más 'and moreover' · non más 'no more, nothing more'; por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more'
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida) · also es — that (apocopated esse = ese, demonstrative; en es alcaz 'in that pursuit', por es logar 'through that place')
paz: paz — peace (= paz; moros en paz 'Moors at peace', i.e. those who have submitted)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
id: ir — go! (2nd pl. imperative; id vos 'go (you)', with reflexive vos; = id, idos)
medina: Medina — Medinaceli, the frontier town on the Jalón where Alfonso's land ends (= Medinaceli)
quanto: quanto — as much as, whatever (= cuanto) · quanto ella mejor sabe 'as best she can' (quanto + comparative 'as much as') · also 'how much' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'as far/fast as' (quanto pueden andar) · tanto quanto 'as long as'; por quanto … ha 'for all that there is' (por quanto en el mundo ha)
far: far — to do (apocopated infinitive of fazer; = hacer)
mi: mi — my (unstressed possessive) · also mi — me (stressed pronoun after a preposition; por mi 'on my behalf'; = mí)
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
albar: Albar — Álvar (Albar Fáñez, the Cid's lieutenant and kinsman; = Álvar)
así: así — thus, so; así como 'as soon as'
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como) · how, that, in the way that (commo sirva a doña Ximena 'how he is to serve doña Ximena'); like (commo la uña de la carne) · also commo si + imperfect subjunctive — 'as if' (commo si escapasse 'as if he were fleeing') · commo que 'as one who' (commo que ira a de rey … es echado 'as one who has the king's anger and is cast out') · also commo — 'as soon as, when' (commo gelo a dicho 'as soon as he told it him'); 'since, as' (commo fío por Dios 'as I trust in God')
hi: hi — there, in it (adverb, variant of i from Latin ibi; hi gañó a Colada 'there he won Colada'; = allí)
fincaré: fincar — I shall remain (future 1st sg.; = quedaré, closest; modern hincar means 'to drive in')
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men') · also en + infinitive 'in (doing)' (en levarlo adelant 'in carrying it forward'); en çinco días 'in five days'
valençia: Valençia — Valencia, the Moorish kingdom and city whose king Tamín is addressed (= Valencia)
mucho: mucho — much, greatly · also mucho — very, intensifying a predicate (mucho es mañana 'it is much too early, too soon') · also mas mucho — 'more' (mucho as a comparative = más: mas mucho fue provechosa 'was more profitable'; Pidal)
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord') · also ha de + inf. 'is to' (que los ha de aguardar 'who is to attend them'; aver de + infinitive, = ha de)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us') · also si — si'nulla = sin + nulla with -n assimilated before n- (si'nulla dubda 'without any fear' (or 'doubt'); = sin ningún miedo, sin ninguna duda)
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain)
tengo: tener — I hold (present 1st sg.; en grado vos lo tengo 'I hold it to you in thanks', I am grateful; = tengo) · also tener que — 'I think that' (tengo que vos avrá pro 'I think he will be of use to you'; = creo que)
heredad: heredad — inherited holding, estate, landed property (por heredad 'as a possession'; = heredad)
era: seer — it was (imperfect of seer = ser) · era + past part. 'had' (ser as pluperfect auxiliary with intransitives; Minaya assí era llegado 'Minaya had arrived')
dicho: dezir — said (past part.; a dicho = ha dicho, 'he has said')
pienssan: pensar — they think; pensar de + inf. 'to set about (doing)' (epic formula)
andar: andar — to travel, go on (infinitive; = andar)
albergar: albergar — to lodge, halt for the night (infinitive; iva albergar 'went to lodge', i.e. lodged; = albergar, closest alojarse, acampar)
otro: otro — other, another (masc.; el otro 'the other'; = otro) · also otro día 'the next day'; lo otro 'the rest'
posar: posar — to lodge, halt for the night (infinitive; = posar)
saliólos: salir + los — he went out to (them) (preterite salió + enclitic los; saliólos reçebir 'went out to welcome them'; = salió a recibirlos)
faze: fazer — is done, is made (present 3rd sg.; = hace) · also fazer — he does, makes (active present 3rd sg.; por tal lo faze mio Çid 'for that reason Mio Cid does it'; = hace)
venides: venir — you come (2nd pl. present, old -des ending; = venís)
myo: mio — my (unstressed possessive, variant spelling of mio)
natural: natural — natural, rightful, by birth (adjective; señor natural 'a rightful lord, one owed allegiance by birth'; = natural)
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
pesa: pesar — it grieves, it distresses (present 3rd sg., impersonal; mucho pesa a los de Teca 'it greatly grieves the men of Ateca'; = pesa)
sabet: saber — know, mark you (imperative 2nd pl., sabed; sabet = sabed; epic tag addressed to the audience)
plaze: plazer — it pleases (present 3rd sg., impersonal; non plaze 'it does not please, they dislike it'; = place)
fabló: fablar — he spoke (preterite; = habló, note f-)
mandólo: mandar + lo — he ordered it (mandó 3rd sg. preterite + object lo, the accent written on the verb's stressed vowel; mandólo y çercar 'he had him (the Cid; or 'it', the place) besieged there'; = lo mandó)
acorrades: acorrer — you help (present subjunctive 2nd pl., -ades; commo la acorrades 'how you succour it, i.e. the banner'; = acorráis, socorráis)
están: estar — they are, stay (present 3rd pl.; = están) · also progressive auxiliary with a gerund (bendiziéndol están 'they are blessing him')
ellas: ella — they, them (fem. pl., stressed; con ellas 'with them'; = ellas)
gelas: ge + las — them for/to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + las; = se las)
acá: acá — here, hither (adverb; exidos somos acá 'we have come out to here'; = acá)
dellas: de + ellas — of them, about them (contraction, fem. pl.)
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
fer: fazer — to do, make (short infinitive form; = hacer; fer lo he = lo haré, split future)
he: aver — I have (1st sg. present; perfect auxiliary, = he, and the auxiliary of the split future, e.g. doblar vos he)
noch: noche — night (apocopated form of noche; cf. anoch)
conducho: conducho — provisions, victuals (Latin conductus; covers everything an army eats)
les: les — to them · also les — 'from them', dative of removal or injury (les tollió el pan 'took the bread from them'; viédales exir 'forbids them to go out')
dio: dar — he gave, struck (preterite 3rd sg.; un colpe dio 'he struck a blow'; = dio) · dar a + inf. 'to give (something) to be …-ed' (Dio a partir estos dineros 'he had this money shared out') · also dar — he dispatched, sent (Pidal: 'despachó, envió'; Dio tres cavalleros 'he dispatched three knights'; = envió)
mañana: mañana — morning (a la mañana 'in the morning'; otro dia mañana 'next morning'; = mañana) · also mañana — early, soon (adverb/predicate; mucho es mañana 'it is too soon (to take back a man in disgrace after only three weeks)'; = pronto, temprano)
mas: mas — but · also mas — 'most' (superlative, = más; en todo lo mas alto 'on the very highest part') · also mas — 'more' comparative (que es mas ondrada 'which is more honored'; = más)
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
va: ir — he/she goes (present 3rd sg.; = va); ir + gerund, 'to be (gradually) doing' · ir + infinitive 'goes to' (la manol va besar 'goes to kiss his hand', el Duero va passar 'goes to cross the Duero') · also va — 'there is, goes on' impersonal (¡Qué priessa va en los moros! 'what a stir there is among the Moors!')
passan: passar — they cross, pass (present 3rd pl.; = pasan)
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
fieras: fiero — great, mighty, extraordinary (fem. pl.; fieras ganançias 'great gains'; modern fiero 'fierce', so a weaker sense here (uncertain nuance); = grandes)
passaron: passar — they passed, crossed (preterite 3rd pl.; = pasaron)
desí: desí — from there, thence; thereupon (adverb, des + i 'there'; e desí arriba 'and from there upward'; = desde allí, después) · also desí — next, then in a series (desí a Molina 'next Molina')
taranz: Taranz — campo de Taranz, part of the plateau dividing the waters of the Tajuña and the Jalón, on the border of the provinces of Guadalajara and Soria (Pidal)
guisa: guisa — manner, fashion; a guisa de 'in the fashion of' · a vuestra guisa 'as you see fit, in your own way' (prended a vuestra guisa 'take as you please') · also de guisa que 'in such a way that' (de guisa irán por ellas que … 'in such a manner will they go for them that …'; = de modo que)
ningún: ninguno — no, any (apocopated masc. sg. before a noun; ningún omne 'no man'; = ningún)
han: aver — they have (present 3rd pl.; = han); after an infinitive, the auxiliary of a split future (seervos han = os serán) · also han a + inf. 'they have to, are bound to' (mandado de so señor todo lo han a far); 'they hold, possess' (que moros las han) · also perfect auxiliary 'have' with a participle agreeing with its object (la ganançia que han fecha 'the booty they have made')
val: valer — help! (imperative 2nd sg., apocopated for vale; = vale) · val — valley (noun, = valle; el val de río Martín 'the valley of the river Martín') · also valer — he helps, avails (present 3rd sg., apocopated for vale; si no nos val 'if he does not help us'; = vale)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
recabdo: recabdo — care, precaution, strict order (= recaudo) · also recabdo — business secured, a sure outcome (con todo buen recabdo 'with everything well in hand') · recabdo — account, reckoning (oro e plata que non saben recabdo 'gold and silver past all reckoning') · also con recabdo — within bounds, under control (non es con recabdo el dolor de Valençia 'the grief of Valencia is past all bounds')
vídolos: ver + los — he saw them (vido 3rd sg. preterite + object los, the accent written on the verb's stressed vowel; = los vio)
alvar: Alvar — Álvar (Fáñez), the Cid's kinsman and lieutenant ('Minaya')
sopiessen: saber — (so that) they might know (imperfect subjunctive 3rd pl.; = supiesen/supieran)
verdad: verdad — truth (dezir vos he la verdad 'I shall tell you the truth'; = verdad) · also non será verdad — 'it shall not be so' (Pidal: 'esto no será así'; esto non será verdad)
detardan: detardar — they delay (present 3rd pl.; cf. detardava)
uno: uno — one; en uno = 'together, as one' · el uno ... el otro 'the one ... the other' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró)
fincó: fincar — he planted, set firm (preterite; fincar los inojos 'to kneel') · also fincar — he stayed, remained (el Campeador fincó con su mesnada 'the Cid stayed with his troop'; = quedó)
ellos: ellos — they, them (stressed 3rd pl. masc. pronoun)
y: y — and (rarer spelling of e) · also y — there (adverb, = i, Latin ibi; entraré y 'I shall enter there')
virtos: virtos — uncertain word, probably 'forces, hosts' (pl.; creçen estos virtos 'these forces grow'; perhaps from Latin virtus; the exact sense is doubtful)
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision) · also nos — non + se, written without apostrophe (nin amigo a amigo nos pueden consolar 'nor can friend console friend'; mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him', the no redundant after the comparison)
buscar: buscar — to seek (infinitive; buscar nos verná 'he will come to seek us'; buscar nos ie 'he would seek us', infinitive + clitic + auxiliary, split future/conditional; = buscar)
afevos: afevos — behold, here is/are (presentative, a + fe + vos; = he aquí, ahí tenéis)
aquí: aquí — here; d'aquí 'from here' · also 'then, at this point' (aquí dixo el comde 'then the count said')
quieren: querer — they wish, are about to (present 3rd pl.)
sin: sin — without · also sin — 'besides, apart from' (sin las peonadas 'besides the foot-soldiers'); sin falla 'without fail'; sin dubda
hart: hart — uncertain: Pidal's note on this line reads it as art, 'trick, flaw, loophole' (sin art 'without deceit', then 'perfectly'; 'non i avía art' = 'there was no defect', the siege was perfect); = arte, closest 'falla, resquicio'
martin: Martín — Martín (personal name; Martin Muñoz, governor of Mont Mayor; same as martín, here without accent)
sues: su — his, her (fem. pl. possessive, old sue/sues; = sus)
fuerças: fuerça — force, might; pl. forces, strong troops (por estas fuerças 'through these forces', i.e. among these hosts; = fuerzas)
sabor: sabor — pleasure, wish; a so sabor 'at his (their) pleasure'
dar: dar — to give (infinitive; split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos) · also dar salto 'to make a dash, sally' (salto davan); dar çevada 'to give barley, feed the horses' · also dar — to give way, yield (oviéronse a dar 'they had to give way'; = ceder, rendirse)
essora: essora — then, at that moment (ess' + ora; en essora 'at that moment'; = entonces)
vayamos: ir — let us go (present subjunctive 1st pl., exhortative; = vayamos)
esso: esso — that (neuter demonstrative; esso con esto 'that together with this'; = eso)
detardar: detardar — to delay, put off (infinitive; non lo quiso detardar 'he would not put it off'; = tardar, demorar)
salieron: salir — they went out (preterite 3rd pl.; = salieron)
den: den — from there, from it (de + en, the short form of ende 'thence', as dent = de + ent; non pueden den quitar 'they cannot get clear of it'; = de allí, de ello)
mal: mal — harm, hurt, ruin · mal — evil, in the prayer's sense (por end es salvo de mal 'therefore he is saved from evil') · also mal — adverb 'sorely, ill' (por cuer le pesó mal 'it grieved him sorely at heart') · also tener a mal — 'to take amiss' (non lo tenga a mal 'let him not take it amiss')
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding · a las manos 'for the hands' (pidió agua a las manos 'asked for water to wash his hands'); bolver las manos 'to ply the hands', busy eating
lanças: lança — lance; also the horseman who bears it (pl.; = lanzas)
pendones: pendón — pennon, lance-banner (men are counted by lances)
qué: qué — what a …! (exclamative) · also qué — what? which? (interrogative pronoun/adjective, as in de qué será pagado, 'with what will he be satisfied') · indirect: que non sabe qué se far '(so that) she knows not what to do'; avemos qué fablar 'we have something to speak of' · also qué — how (exclamative before an adverb: qué bien pago 'how well he paid')
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?') · also o — where (relative adverb; o dizen Castejón 'which they call Castejón'; o el Campeador estava 'where the Campeador was'; = donde) · correlative 'either … or' (o me dexaredes … o … levaredes 'either you will leave me … or you will take away')
quomo: commo — as (variant spelling, Pidal's Qu[o]mo; = como)
ivan: ir — they were going (imperfect 3rd pl.; ivan posar 'they were going to lodge'; = iban) · also ir + gerund, 'were coming to, gradually' (ya lo ivan provando 'they were by now coming to experience it')
armas: arma — weapon, arms (pl.; armas de lidiar 'weapons for fighting'; en armas 'in arms, armed'; = armas) · also armas — men-at-arms, armed men (treynta mill de armas 'thirty thousand armed men')
çerca: çerca — near; here adverbial, çerca o tarde = 'sooner or later' (= cerca) · also çerca — siege, encirclement (noun; en çerca 'under siege'; = cerco) · also çercar — he besieges (present 3rd sg.; bien la çerca mio Çid 'my Çid besieges it well'; = cerca)
salón: Salón — the river Jalón (the old form of the name; = Jalón)
gozos: gozo — joy, rejoicing (masc. pl.; grandes son los gozos 'great is the rejoicing'; = gozos)
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing') · also ir + infinitive 'go to' (le van çercar 'they go to besiege him'; se van tornar 'they go back')
dont: dont — from where, whence (Latin de unde; = de donde, donde); also temporal, 'when, as soon as' (dont a ojo los ovo 'as soon as he had them in sight')
ojo: ojo — eye; a ojo 'in plain sight'
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira') · lo so — 'what is his, his own' (neuter article + possessive; lo so puede menguar 'what is his may dwindle') · also so — their (so consejo 'their counsel', so vino 'their wine'; = su)
convusco: con + vusco — with you (fused form; cf. con vusco, v. 75)
lidiador: lidiador — fighter, warrior (agent noun from lidiar; closest luchador, combatiente)
ffijas: fija — daughter (pl.; variant spelling with ff of fijas; = hijas)
naturales: natural — natural, by blood, true-born (adjective, pl.; mis fijas naturales 'my daughters by birth'; = naturales; Pidal's bracketed supplied word)
hemos: aver — we will/shall (1st pl. future auxiliary; restored by Pidal in the split future dar gelos [hemos] = se los daremos)
auze: auze — luck, fortune (vuestra auze 'your good fortune'; a word of augury, usually traced to Latin avis 'bird'; rare, and its exact sense not certain; closest suerte, ventura)
maguer: maguer — although (a rare word, of Greek origin)
le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him') · also le — dative of separation, 'from him' (que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'); dative 'for him' (ques le non spidiés 'who does not take leave of him')
queramos: querer — we may wish (present subjunctive 1st pl.; que nos queramos ir 'if we should want to go', que + subjunctive as a condition; = queramos)
gelo: ge + lo — it to him/them (ge, ancestor of modern se, + lo; = se lo)
podremos: poder — we shall be able (future 1st pl.; = podremos)
